1. **F1 — blocking, issue-impact:** Applying over a torn `events.jsonl` tail cannot succeed. The service intentionally turns a torn prefix into a separate physical line, then validates that exact overlay before publishing ([profile.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-9b0a997e/crates/jit/src/commands/profile.rs:123), [profile.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-9b0a997e/crates/jit/src/commands/profile.rs:133)). Repository validation rejects every non-empty line that is not JSON ([repository.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-9b0a997e/crates/jit/src/validation/repository.rs:652)), so `{"torn":\n<event>\n` fails before the transaction. This violates REQ-02’s required torn-tail preservation/application behavior and leaves REQ-03’s service-level torn-tail case untested.

2. **F2 — blocking, issue-impact:** The new public command-layer entrypoint bypasses the universal recovery boundary. `apply_embedded_profile` creates a kernel and immediately calls the mutation method ([profile.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-9b0a997e/crates/jit/src/commands/profile.rs:59)); that method only acquires the repository/event locks ([profile.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-9b0a997e/crates/jit/src/commands/profile.rs:74)). It never invokes or requires `RecoveryCoordinator::recover_before_services`, unlike the established mutation startup path ([main.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-9b0a997e/crates/jit/src/main.rs:1731)). Consequently a direct library caller can apply over a pending journal; the added tests recover only through an explicit manual call after dropping the executor ([profile.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-9b0a997e/crates/jit/src/commands/profile.rs:406)).
